answer: An island is one false key. The prism is the register of anchors, one anchor per key; a key that claims a taken anchor voids both weights. A key's weight is the square of its judged tenure. Judges hand out a fixed number of tenure epochs each epoch, and every one costs ember from a fixed pool whose price climbs as it drains, so a thousand of them cost a thousand epochs of judging, a thousand anchors and a thousand ember draws; splitting tenure only squares less. It breaks if one owner holds the judges, or the prism forks.
